judged_text: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed object keys `[z.string().toString()]`, which evaluate to the literal key "ZodString" (or similar), so the schema does not allow arbitrary extra properties like refresh_token, expiry_date, or scope at all. When credential sharing is enabled, every provider refresh response is parsed against a schema requiring a property literally named "ZodString" to be a number and permitting nothing else; zod's default strips unknown keys, so parsed data contains only access_token (and drops refresh_token, expiry_date, instance_url, etc.), which callers then read as undefined — Google reads token.expiry_date as undefined and Zoho/Salesforce lose instance_url, producing broken credentials written to the DB.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. In JS/TS these expressions evaluate immediately to literal strings (e.g. "ZodString"/"ZodOptional"), so the schema does **not** accept arbitrary token-response properties like `expiry_date`, `expires_in`, `scope`, `instance_url`, etc. When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, `parseRefreshTokenResponse()` uses this schema, which will either fail parsing real provider responses (throwing "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned") or not validate/retain the expected fields. This is directly introduced by the diff.
